original_strict_contract: identity H requires exactly zero; preserved rejected native trial and valid original CUDA.jl five-trial series
derivation: For the measured identity-H fixture, every output component has only two nonzero opposite products d*x and x*d, with all remaining products exactly zero. Imaginary H is zero. The companion sigma component is selected by the source complex -i commutator.

Let RN32 denote round-to-nearest-even binary32. With separate multiply/add, RN32(d*x)-RN32(x*d)=0. With multiply-add contraction, the residual is RN32(RN32(d*x)-exact(d*x)) or its negative according to source update order. Both initial products contracted into zero still round to RN32(d*x).

Two binary32 significands have at most 48 product bits, so exact(d*x) is representable in binary64 for these finite normal-range inputs. Hence r=RN32(binary64(RN32(binary64(d)*binary64(x)))-binary64(d)*binary64(x)) is independently computable without GPU outputs.

The auxiliary acceptance set is exactly {0,+r,-r} componentwise, implying the independently derived componentwise bound abs(output)<=abs(r). No global tolerance is fitted to observed GPU residuals. IDs 1 and 2 use unscaled identity d=1, so r=0 before final HDT scaling.
AoS companion component is zero-based index xor 1. AoSoA4 companion index is package*392+element*8+(1-component)*4+lane. IDs 4..23 use AoSoA4; all other numeric IDs use AoS.
All original full-output Float64 oracle comparisons (atol 1e-6, rtol 1e-4), guards, bit-exact input checks, execution-only scope, launch counts and timing regions remain unchanged.
scope: Only declared real identity-H inputs and original source operation orders; no universal compiler or arbitrary complex-H error bound.
